question:
Two thin convex lenses $L_1$ and $L_2$ of focal lengths $f_1=10\,\text{cm}$ and $f_2=20\,\text{cm}$ are placed coaxially in air with separation $d$ (distance between optical centres). An object is placed $15\,\text{cm}$ to the left of $L_1$ on the common principal axis. Use Cartesian sign convention with positive direction to the right.

(i) The separation $d$ is adjusted such that after refraction through both lenses, the emergent rays from $L_2$ are parallel (final image at infinity).

(ii) Keeping this same separation $d$, the object is shifted along the axis by a distance $x$ (take $x>0$ if the object is moved towards $L_1$) so that the final image is formed at a distance $60\,\text{cm}$ to the right of $L_2$.

The pair $(x,\,M)$, where $M$ is the net transverse magnification in case (ii), is closest to:
